brief: The 8 multi-agent patterns every AI builder needs — supervisor, swarm, feedback loop, more.

slots.body: Single models hit context and reasoning ceilings. These patterns show how to split, route, and synthesize work across specialized agents without orchestration chaos.
A central agent delegates subtasks to specialist workers, then synthesizes outputs into a coherent final result.
slots.card1Body: Complex workflows requiring strict control, tool use, and centralized error handling.
slots.card2Body: The supervisor is a router and reducer, not merely a passive dispatcher.

slots.body: Identical agents process data chunks independently in parallel, with an aggregator merging results downstream.
slots.card1Body: High-throughput tasks like scraping, classification, or bulk generation at scale.
slots.card2Body: Homogeneous agents must be stateless and idempotent to avoid race conditions.

slots.body: A generator agent drafts output that a critic agent scores and annotates, triggering iterative refinement cycles.
slots.card1Body: Quality-critical outputs like code review, content editing, or structured data validation.
slots.card2Body: Tight loops converge faster when critics use structured rubrics instead of vague scores.

slots.body: An intake agent classifies incoming requests and routes each to the single best-fit specialist agent downstream.
slots.card1Body: Multi-domain systems where no single model excels at every user intent.
slots.card2Body: Accurate routing reduces token waste and prevents specialist context pollution.

slots.body: Large tasks split into independent subtasks, executed concurrently, then reduced into a unified final answer.
slots.card1Body: Long-context jobs like document analysis or multi-source research synthesis.
slots.card2Body: Map-Reduce beats monolithic prompts on latency and context-window limits.

slots.body: A planner agent decomposes goals into dependent subtasks, assigns workers dynamically, and assembles the output.
slots.card1Body: Multi-step coding, research, or tool chains with conditional branching logic.
slots.card2Body: Dynamic replanning outperforms static DAGs when tools fail or requirements shift.

slots.body: Start with the topology that matches your latency, cost, and accuracy constraints today.
slots.quote: Multi-agent is a topology choice, not a model upgrade.
